                "user_id": "has(hop.user_id) ? hop.user_id : ''",
                "audience_set": "'[\"agent:%s\",\"member:%s\"]'" % (agent, person),
                # GH #972 (R-NL-4) -- the round this turn is BORN in, a second
                # time under a key no config's own edge may set
                # (`STAMPED_CONTEXT_KEYS`, the mutation door and the boot pass
                # refuse it): `audience_set` is rewritten by many a template on
                # the way, and an app's inner edge could write it too. The
                # curator places an app's pin in its own round only when that
                # round is this one (`templates/curator/README.md`).
                "turn_round": "'[\"agent:%s\",\"member:%s\"]'" % (agent, person)}}}
    if bound is not None:
        # GH #949 -- the speaker, only with a sender proof (see `_speaker`).
        ingress["modifier"]["set_context"]["speaker"] = _speaker(person, bound)
    elif (_template_name(p.get("template")) in PROXY_IDENTITY_CHANNELS
          and p.get(BIND_USER_KEY) is not None):
        # GH #979 -- a web session: the proof is the proxy's identity header,
        # which the cell carries as `hop.user_id`; the same expression as a
        # named sender on a bound chat, so one reader serves both.
        user = _binding(p.get(BIND_USER_KEY), BIND_USER_KEY, BIND_USER_QUESTION)
        ingress["modifier"]["set_context"]["speaker"] = _speaker(person, (None, user))
    return [
        ingress,
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.error_code)",
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'error'"}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'answer' && "
                      "has(context.channel_node) && "
                      "context.channel_node == '%s'" % name},
        # GH #803 -- the mirror of the delegation door one container over, and
        # the same rule: `member@1.9.0` re-stamps the three advice sections
        # (`fact`, `context`, `correction`) onto `./channels` as `in_advise`,
        # addressed by `context.channel_node`, and a lane addressed at a
        # container reaches nobody until the container carries it. Same shape as
        # the `answer` edge above, because it is the same question -- which of
        # this member's channels is this for -- and a second spelling of one
        # address is a second thing to keep in step.
        #
        # It is rendered for EVERY channel and not only for one whose cell
        # accepts the lane, which is the table's own doctrine (WHY A TABLE AND
        # NOT A DERIVATION, above): the set is a property of the PARENT. It
        # costs nothing where the child cannot use it. A section only exists
        # because the front model was told to write one, and it is told that
        # only in `advise` mode -- which the collector switches on for
        # `context.engine == 'duplex'` and for nothing else. Without this edge
        # the section dead-letters at the container; with it, on a channel that
        # never produces one, nothing travels at all.
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'in_advise' && "
                      "has(context.channel_node) && "
                      "context.channel_node == '%s'" % name},
    ]


def _screen_level(place, name, _p):
    # A screen is a channel too -- and it costs three edges, one fewer than a
    # chat channel since `member@1.9.0` because nothing advises a display,
    # though the third points the OTHER way: what only a screen
    # produces is `event` and `receipt`, and what a screen TAKES is a view,
    # re-stamped onto the display's own lane, and -- since 1.10.0 -- the
    # failures of the channels beside it, re-stamped `in_notice` (GH #680, ADR
    # 0039). An agent's prose `answer` is NOT a view (GH #598): the display
    # reads a view out of the body and refuses a document that carries none, so
    # binding the answer here bought one refusal per answer and, before #598,
    # one turn per refusal.
    #
    # GH #522 -- both keys, and on a screen they carry the same word. A screen
    # IS one room, so its address and its conversation partner coincide; writing
    # the identity out anyway is what lets every holder downstream go on reading
    # `channel` and every answer go on routing by `channel_node`, whichever kind
    # of channel it came from.
    #
    # GH #645 -- and the VIEWER, where the display was given an
    # `identity_header`: the header the proxy sent rides as `hop.user_id` on
    # every semantic browser event, and a `hop` is single-hop, so a stamp this
    # edge does not promote is gone one storey up. Same guarded form as the chat
    # connector's ingress edge (`has(...) ? ... : ''`), for the same reason: a
    # modifier that fails to evaluate skips the WHOLE edge, and a screen with no
    # identity header stamps no `user_id` at all.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt')",
         "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % name,
                                      "channel": "'%s'" % name,
                                      "user_id": "has(hop.user_id) ? hop.user_id : ''"}}},
        # GH #709 -- and the WITHDRAWAL beside the view, in the SAME edge with one
        # ternary. A view outlives the turn that produced it, so ending one is a
        # message (`display` has accepted `in_withdraw` since it shipped) -- and
        # `member@1.8.0` carries `withdraw` out of `./apps` beside `view`. Without
        # this half the lane ends in the container: the first withdrawal of an app
        # with several views is a `no_route` in the DLQ, once per withdrawal. One
        # edge and not two, because the two are one lane pair of one producer.
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) "
                      "&& (hop.route == 'view' || hop.route == 'withdraw') "
                      "&& has(context.channel_node) "
                      "&& context.channel_node == '%s'" % name,
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {
             "route": "hop.route == 'withdraw' ? 'in_withdraw' : 'in_view'"}}},
        # GH #680 -- the error wire IN. A channel's `error` leaves the
        # container upwards for the operator (the member's own edge) AND
        # reaches the screen as a system notice. No `channel_node` guard: an
        # error carries no context of the screen, it belongs to the member,
        # and every channel failure in this container is a notice for that
        # member's screen. The screen itself never emits `error`, so this
        # cannot loop. The container knows its screen only through the
        # mutation that grows it, which is why the edge is drawn here and not
        # in the member template.
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'error'",
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_notice'"}}},
    ]


def _app_level(place, name, p):
    # An app writes onto ONE screen, and what comes back is addressed by the
    # OWNER the display stamped -- the path of the cell that put the view up,
    # never anything the body claims. `hop.owner` is an ABSOLUTE path, so the
    # container stays in the guard whatever the declaration's scope is.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'view' || hop.route == 'error')",
         "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % p["screen"],
                                      "channel": "'%s'" % p["screen"]}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt') "
                      "&& has(hop.owner) && hop.owner.contains('/%s/%s/')"
                      % (place.container, name)},
        # GH #553 -- the mutation receipt. An app draws a picture of something,
        # and the only thing that changes what a picture of a colony shows is a
        # committed mutation; the shipped app (`colony-view`) turns the lane
        # into its own `in_refresh` and the BOOT receipt is what puts the first
        # picture up. It carries no name guard, because an app is addressed by
        # the `hop.owner` the display stamped and a receipt has no owner -- the
        # container and assistant hops of this lane DO carry the permissive name
        # guard (GH #478), and it is the context-less receipt that makes all
        # three of them a fan-out rather than an address.
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'mutation_committed'"},
    ]


# level -> (container it is instantiated into, renderer, extra required params).
# The container is part of the table rather than a parameter: a member does not
# stand in `./people` in one colony and `./members` in another, and a level that
# could be told where it lives would stop being a level. Since GH #503 it is
# also the level's SCOPE, which is the same statement read as an address.
LEVELS = {
    "org":       ("orgs",       _container_level, []),
    "member":    ("members",    _container_level, []),
    "assistant": ("assistants", _assistant_level, []),
    "channel":   ("channels",   _channel_level,   ["assistant"]),
    "screen":    ("channels",   _screen_level,    []),
    "app":       ("apps",       _app_level,       ["screen"]),
}


def grow_level(p, settings=None):
    level = p["level"]
    container, render, _extra = LEVELS[level]
    # GH #560 -- a generation may be grown with NO key of its own. The switch is
    # opt-in for the same reason the identity door is: writing a person's
    # provider credential into an agent's reach is not something a level does to
    # every generation grown from it without being asked.
    # GH #1061: a member is grown with grants too -- its memory hive and file
    # space call providers, and since #801 nothing else hands them a key.
    # The member's SCREEN (`display`) judges with a model as well; it is grown
    # by `member_devices` and takes the member's credential wish along.
    # GH #1061 (OR-VG.V4.5): and a channel that spends a key (CHANNEL_GRANTS).
    credential = (p.get("credential")
                  if level in ("assistant", "member", "screen", "channel") else None)
    # The narrow form for every level, and the two exceptions are reachability
    # facts rather than a taste. An identity door reaches the container's
    # SIBLING `./affinity`, which no declaration standing in the container can
    # name -- written out at the branch that draws it, in `_assistant_level`.
    # The credential road reaches the member's own `./access`, one storey up in
    # the same way. An edge lives in the graph of the lowest common ancestor of
    # its endpoints, so either switch moves the whole declaration to the member.
    place = Place(container, not ((level == "assistant"
                                   and (p.get("subscribe") or credential))
                                  or (level in ("screen", "channel")
                                      and credential)))
    node = {"name": place.node(p["name"]), "template": p["template"]}
    if isinstance(p.get("override_params"), dict):
        node["override_params"] = p["override_params"]
    channel_grants = (_channel_grants(p, credential)
                      if credential and level == "channel" else None)
    if channel_grants:
        own = _channel_credential_overrides(node.get("override_params"),
                                            channel_grants)
        if own:
            node["override_params"] = own
    elif credential:
        node["override_params"] = _credential_overrides(
            node.get("override_params"), p["name"], credential, p["template"], level)
    # The birth state travels TOP-LEVEL on the entry, beside `template` and not
    # inside `override_params`: it is a property of the placement and not of a
    # cell's own settings, it covers the whole subtree the node brings, and the
    # door reads it exactly there (GH #472).
    birth = p.get("birth") or LEVEL_BIRTH.get(level)
    if birth:
        node["birth"] = birth
    # ONE declaration, and since GH #567 that holds for the credential road too:
    # the node, its edges and the grants that answer them are one decision, and
    # a manifest rolls forward with no rollback -- a node that landed without
    # its edges is an island, which is the failure this recipe exists to
    # prevent. The credential edges come LAST, behind the level's own, and the
    # grants ride in the same diff.
    ctx = p.get("ctx") if isinstance(p.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
    diff = {"add_nodes": [node], "add_edges": render(place, p["name"], p)}
    now = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
           .strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"))
    if credential and level in ("assistant", "screen"):
        diff["add_edges"] = (diff["add_edges"]
                             + _credential_edges(p["name"], credential,
                                                 p["template"], level,
                                                 prefix=place.down(p["name"]) + "/"))
        diff["seed_rows"] = _credential_rows(p["name"], credential, now,
                                             p["template"], level)
    if channel_grants:
        # The ask is not a turn: a self-bound channel's ingress takes every
        # emission without an error code, and the cell's `credential_request`
        # would reach the container as one (a bound one requires a chat id,
        # which the ask does not carry). The ingress is the level's FIRST edge.
        ingress = diff["add_edges"][0]
        ingress["condition"] = ("!(has(hop.route) && hop.route == "
                                "'credential_request') && " + ingress["condition"])
        diff["add_edges"] = (diff["add_edges"]
                             + _channel_credential_edges(place, p["name"],
                                                         channel_grants))
        diff["seed_rows"] = _channel_credential_rows(p["name"], credential, now,
                                                     channel_grants)
    # GH #835 -- the member's door, last of all (see DOOR_LEVELS above). The
    # switch is `True` and nothing else: a truthy string drew a door for
    # `"door": "false"` (review of #835, Minor 2); the refusal below names it.
    if level in DOOR_LEVELS and p.get("door") is True:
        diff["add_edges"] = diff["add_edges"] + [_door_edge(place, p["name"])]
    out = [{"scope": place.scope(p["scope"]), "ctx": ctx, "diff": diff}]
    # GH #1061 -- a member's consumers and its broker are both INSIDE the node
    # this declaration creates, so their edges live in the member's own graph:
    # a second declaration scoped at the newborn member, in the same manifest.
    # Its cells ask on their first provider call, never at birth, so the grants
    # one entry later are there before anything asks.
    if credential and level == "member":
        here = "%s/%s" % (place.scope(p["scope"]).rstrip("/"), place.node(p["name"]))
        out.append({"scope": here, "ctx": ctx, "diff": {
            "add_edges": _credential_edges(p["name"], credential, p["template"],
                                           level, prefix="./"),
            "seed_rows": _credential_rows(p["name"], credential, now,
                                          p["template"], level)}})
    if level in REGISTRY_BRAINS:
        out += _model_registry(p, ctx, settings or {})
    return out


# --- the model registry's road (GH #855) ---------------------------------------
#
# In a colony with an `llm-registry`, every brain an assistant is grown with is a
# SUBSCRIBER of it: the registry resolves a model package per brain and pushes it
# through the composite's `in_model` door. Since GH #858 a member is one too:
# the four llm cells of its memory hive, through that hive's door, and every
# announced brain carries the prose need of its template cell, which the
# registry translates against its catalogue. Two things make a brain one, and a
# level can render both -- the rows cannot be written by it, see below:
#
#   * the PUSH edges, one per brain: from the container the registry's pushes
#     arrive at (`meclaw-os` carries `update` from `./llm-registry` into
#     `./orgs`, restamped `in_model`) down to the brain's composite, addressed by
#     `hop.subscriber` -- the brain's cell path. `Edge.to` is a static path, so
#     N brains cost N edges, the address rule this recipe keeps everywhere.
#   * the ANNOUNCEMENT, one edge per generation: every mutation receipt that
#     reaches the generation (GH #553, the permissive door above) also leaves it
#     for the container as `model_subscribe`, carrying the brains and their start
#     values in `context.model_announced` and the generation itself in
#     `context.model_generation`, and `meclaw-os` hands that to the registry's
#     `in_hand`. So the row appears AFTER the commit that made the cell, and a
#     lost row comes back with the next receipt or the boot's.
#
# Both are FORMS the submit gate checks (`model_road_form_error`): a push edge
# carries only the pushes addressed to one cell directly in its composite, and an
# announcement edge is drawn only in the manifest that grows its generation.
# Neither writes a hop key the road is addressed by (`subscriber`,
# `subscribe`): the gate refuses that on every edge, because a hop key
# survives a transit through a foreign hive and a context key cannot be
# written by anything but an edge.
#
# WHY NOT A ROW IN THE MANIFEST. The registry stands at `/os/llm-registry`, and a
# `seed_rows` into its store would widen this manifest's scope ROOT to `/os`,
# which the shipped broker refuses (`colony.mutate.default` is scoped
# `/os/orgs`, the shell-wide row ships disabled). The same holds for an edge out
# of `/os/llm-registry`. So both edges stand at the container scope, which the
# broker already permits, and the row is the registry's own write.
#
# WHY A SECOND DECLARATION. The edges live in the graph of the container scope
# (`model_registry_scope`), two to four storeys above the one the level stands
# in, and a declaration has exactly one scope. It travels behind the level in
# the same manifest, so the door rolls it forward against the tree the level
# just grew.
#
# SWITCHED BY THE INSTANCE. `model_registry_scope` is a setting of this cell,
# empty by default: a builder in a tree with no registry renders nothing extra,
# and a brain there keeps its start value (and the substrate's params road).
# `meclaw-os` sets it on its builder ref, because it is the tree that carries one.
#
# The brains a level brings, per shipped template: (composite under the
# generation, the llm cell in it, where its start value comes from, the cell
# of the template whose `params.requirement` it announces). A start value is
# `("ctx", key)` when the manifest's ctx carries it -- the assistant's three
# brains are born on a ctx model key -- or `("env", token)` when the cell reads
# it from the environment itself: the member's memory cells are born on a
# MODEL_ environment token, and the announcement carries the same token, bound
# by the same environment when the manifest is applied (GH #858). A token with
# no default is announced with an empty one: an unset key must not fail the
# whole growth at the door on an edge, where the cell would only have failed
# to boot. The tokens are spelled in two pieces (`ENV` and the braced rest),
# and this comment names none whole, because the colony binds every
# environment token in THIS script when it reads the cell's config -- written
# whole, the announcement would carry what the builder saw at its own boot,
# and an unset key would read as no start value at all.
ENV = "$"
REGISTRY_BRAINS = {
    # OR-KX-P5 (GH #877): each rim's curator summarizer (`curator@1.11.1`) is a
    # subscriber too. It is born on the core's start value (the `model` key of the ctx),
    # and without the announcement it would stay there -- the strongest model
    # doing the cheapest job; announced with its need, the registry picks for
    # the need. Its push rides onto the rim it stands behind, whose `in_model`
    # door hands it on to the curator.
    "assistant": ("assistants", (
        ("talky", "brain", ("ctx", "model_surface"), "talky/brain"),
        ("talky-chat", "brain", ("ctx", "model_surface"), "talky/brain"),
        ("cogny", "brain", ("ctx", "model"), "cogny/brain"),
        ("talky", "curator/summarizer", ("ctx", "model"), "curator/summarizer"),
        ("talky-chat", "curator/summarizer", ("ctx", "model"), "curator/summarizer"),
        ("cogny", "curator/summarizer", ("ctx", "model"), "curator/summarizer"))),
    "member": ("members", (
        ("memory-hive", "closer", ("env", ENV + "{MODEL_CLOSER:-}"), "memory-hive/closer"),
        ("memory-hive", "dialectic", ("env", ENV + "{MODEL_DIALECTIC:-}"), "memory-hive/dialectic"),
        ("memory-hive", "dreamer", ("env", ENV + "{MODEL_DREAMER:-}"), "memory-hive/dreamer"),
        ("memory-hive", "judge", ("env", ENV + "{MODEL_JUDGE:-anthropic/claude-opus-5.5}"),
         "memory-hive/judge"))),
}

def _cel_literal_safe(value):
    # No quote, no backslash, and no raw line break: a CEL string literal cannot
    # hold one, and the submit gate holds the same rule (review of L2a round 4,
    # m-2).
    return isinstance(value, str) and value != "" and "'" not in value \
        and "\\" not in value and "\n" not in value and "\r" not in value


def _announced(entries):
    # Written as it is, like `canonical()`: with `ensure_ascii` a name beyond
    # ASCII became a `\uXXXX` escape -- a backslash inside a CEL literal -- and
    # the submit gate refused the whole growth (review of fix round 2, I-2).
    return json.dumps(entries, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


# Brains the road leaves out, each with its reason. Said on stderr and in the
# recipe's answer after rendering -- a brain that silently stays on its start
# value would read like a subscriber in every document but `show`.
REGISTRY_LEFT_OUT = []


def _model_registry(p, ctx, settings):
    root = str(settings.get("model_registry_scope") or "").rstrip("/")
    if not root:
        return []
    # Only a template that IS the shipped level has these brains, at these
    # places. Another template grown at the same level names its own.
    template = str(p.get("template") or "").split("@", 1)[0]
    if template not in REGISTRY_BRAINS or p.get("level") != template:
        return []
    container, cells = REGISTRY_BRAINS[template]
    gen = "%s/%s/%s" % (str(p["scope"]).rstrip("/"), container, p["name"])
    if not gen.startswith(root + "/"):
        return []
    rel = "./" + gen[len(root) + 1:]
    brains = []
    for rim, cell, (source, key), need in cells:
        start = ctx.get(key) if source == "ctx" else key
        path = "%s/%s/%s" % (gen, rim, cell)
        entry = {"cell_path": path, "start_model": start,
                 "requirement": REQUIREMENTS.get(need, "")}
        # The path is written into the push condition and the entry into the
        # announcement, each between single quotes; the gate holds both to a
        # plain literal. An entry is checked in the form it is written in --
        # JSON escapes a `"` or a control character with a backslash.
        # Each reason names the cause (review of L2a round 4, m-1): a number
        # is a start value that is not a string, and a `'` needs no JSON
        # escape -- it breaks the literal by itself.
        if start is None or start == "":
            why = "no start value in ctx.%s" % key
        elif not isinstance(start, str):
            why = "its start value in ctx.%s is not a string" % key
        elif not _cel_literal_safe(path):
            why = "its path is no plain CEL literal"
        elif not _cel_literal_safe(start):
            # `_cel_literal_safe` refuses a raw line break too (review of the fix
            # strand, m-1), so the reason names it.
            why = "its start value holds a quote, a backslash or a line break"
        elif not _cel_literal_safe(_announced(entry)):
            why = "its start value is no plain CEL literal once written as JSON"
        else:
            brains.append((rim, path, entry))
            continue
        REGISTRY_LEFT_OUT.append({"cell_path": path, "reason": why})
    if not brains:
        return []
    edges = []
    for rim, path, _entry in brains:
        edges.append({"from": ".", "to": "%s/%s" % (rel, rim),
                      "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'in_model' && "
                                   "has(hop.subscriber) && hop.subscriber == '%s'" % path,
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_model'"}}})
    announced = _announced([entry for _rim, _path, entry in brains])
    # The generation this edge speaks for AND the brains it names ride as
    # CONTEXT, which only an edge writes: the registry takes an announcement
    # only for brains inside the generation, and the submit gate lets exactly
    # this form through (review I-1 (iii)). The brains rode on `hop.subscribe`
    # until fix round 2; a hop key survives a hive transit, so a foreign hive
    # on the way back could rewrite them under a true generation stamp.
    edges.append({"from": rel, "to": ".",
                  "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'mutation_committed'",
                  "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'model_subscribe'"},
                               "set_context": {"model_generation": "'%s'" % gen,
                                               "model_announced": "'%s'" % announced}}})
    # GH #863 -- the way back, one edge per composite (talky, talky-chat and
    # cogny of an assistant; the memory hive of a member, whatever number of
    # its cells subscribed), drawn after the announcement: a brain that refuses a push addressed to it sends
    # the refusal out of its composite as `model_refused`, and this edge brings
    # it to the container, where the shell carries it on to the registry's
    # `in_refused`. No modifier -- the submit gate lets exactly this form
    # through (`model_refusal_form`). Without it the refusal dead-letters
    # `no_route` at the composite's parent.
    for rim in sorted({rim for rim, _path, _entry in brains}):
        edges.append({"from": "%s/%s" % (rel, rim), "to": ".",
                      "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'model_refused'"})
    return [{"scope": root, "ctx": {}, "diff": {"add_edges": edges}}]


# GH #963 / PE-DP-11 -- the presenter's decider is a subscriber of the model
# registry, like the brains of a level (its need is the `presenter/decide`
# line of `REQUIREMENTS`): installing the presenter announces
# `<member>/apps/presenter/decide` with its need and no start value (the
# decider is born on its own `model` param, and the registry picks for the need
# alone). Three edges at the registry's container scope, in the forms the
# submit gate already lets through -- the push into the presenter
# (`in_model` addressed to the decider, a leaf one level under it), the
# announcement off the newborn node on `mutation_committed`, and the way back
# of a refusal (`model_refused`). `protocol: "decisions"` tells the registry
# this subscriber takes a decisions endpoint, not a chat model.
def _presenter_registry(p, settings):
    root = str((settings or {}).get("model_registry_scope") or "").rstrip("/")
    if not root or p.get("app") != PRESENTER_APP:
        return []
    node = "%s/apps/%s" % (str(p["scope"]).rstrip("/"), PRESENTER_APP)
    if not node.startswith(root + "/"):
        return []
    rel = "./" + node[len(root) + 1:]
    path = node + "/decide"
    entry = {"cell_path": path, "start_model": "",
             "requirement": REQUIREMENTS["presenter/decide"], "protocol": "decisions"}
    if not _cel_literal_safe(path) or not _cel_literal_safe(_announced([entry])):
        REGISTRY_LEFT_OUT.append({"cell_path": path,
                                  "reason": "its path or entry is no plain CEL literal"})
        return []
    edges = [
        {"from": ".", "to": rel,
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'in_model' && "
                      "has(hop.subscriber) && hop.subscriber == '%s'" % path,
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_model'"}}},
        {"from": rel, "to": ".",
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'mutation_committed'",
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'model_subscribe'"},
                      "set_context": {"model_generation": "'%s'" % node,
                                      "model_announced": "'%s'" % _announced([entry])}}},
        {"from": rel, "to": ".",
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'model_refused'"},
    ]
    return [{"scope": root, "ctx": {}, "diff": {"add_edges": edges}}]

#
# An APP is installed from what it declares. The wiring an app needs at its
# member used to be a manifest somebody wrote by hand -- the member README
# published one, each app repository carried its own, and a live colony was
# repaired twice where the two had drifted apart: the observer edges lost their
# channel guard, `withdraw` joined the view edge, every talky v-lane grew a
# `talky-chat` twin, and a device road appeared that the README never had.
#
# So the app's TEMPLATE carries one block, `template.json` -> `app`, in a closed
# vocabulary of four attachment kinds, and this recipe draws the edges from it.
# The block reaches the recipe INSIDE THE WISH (`params.declaration`), because
# this cell reads nothing but its stdin: no model, no network, no disk -- the
# library answers `/colony/templates` with names and versions and never with a
# block. Whoever places the wish reads the block out of the template and hands
# it over verbatim; that is the role a future `meclaw app install` is given, and
# it is also what an operator or a model does today.
#
# THE SCOPE IS THE MEMBER, not `./apps`: the observer edges start at
# `./firewall`, `./assistants` and `./channels`, the offers end inside a
# generation, a device stands beside the container -- and an edge lives in the
# graph of the lowest common ancestor of its endpoints.
#
# WHAT EACH KIND DRAWS (the counts per declaration live in the builder README):
#
#   screen   -- B4 out of the app, every lane it declares plus `error`, stamped
#               with the screen it draws on; B2 back in, addressed by the
#               `hop.owner` the display stamped. Exactly the two edges
#               `_app_level` draws, with the container in the path.
#   listens  -- one OBSERVER edge into the container per lane, and one binding
#               edge from the container to the app for all of them. The
#               observers are UNGUARDED: an app of a person hears the person's
#               answers whatever carried them, and the answer of an operator's
#               errand too. Because a regular edge suppresses the member's
#               guarded DEFAULT `./assistants -> .` on every case it fires on,
#               the answer observer brings the channel-less exit with it as a
#               regular edge -- without it an answer that names no channel would
#               reach the app and never leave the member. `mutation_committed`
#               needs no observer: the member draws `. -> ./apps` itself.
#               `close` (GH #916) observes the close batch of a session --
#               `write` off `./assistants`, the batch the member's close pass
#               takes too -- and hands it on as `in_close`, restamped on the
#               observer, with the context the close pass carries. `write`
#               already has a regular exit (`./assistants -> .`), so this
#               observer suppresses no default.
#   offers   -- a sidecar is read by name at the container (the member carries
#               every non-`memory` section there); a tool is a v-lane straight
#               from each surface of the generation, guarded on the tool names;
#               every offering cell answers the menu tick on a `schemas` v-lane;
#               and ONE exit stamps who answered. The surfaces are a property of
#               the assistant level (`SURFACE_CALLERS`), like the credential
#               askers are: a tool that only the spoken surface could call would
#               be a tool the typed one never sees.
#   observes_tool_calls
#            -- (GH #937) the call of a named tool, observed on a `tool` v-lane
#               from each surface of the generation into the cell the app names,
#               restamped `in_tool_call` (or the declared route). It is the
#               offer's own edge with another target, drawn as a TAP: whoever
#               offers the tool -- an app or the generation's own `./tools` --
#               still gets the call, the observer gets a copy.
#   observes_tool_results
#            -- the producers of a tool result, observed on v-lanes into the
#               cell the app names. As a string (`"./<cell>"`) every result of
#               the generation's tool hive and of the memory, unstamped (GH
#               #599, kept as it was). As an object (GH #937) only the named
#               tools' results, restamped `in_tool_result` (or the declared
#               route) and named (`tool_name`, the exact name of the call), off
#               every road a result takes into the generation: its tool hive
#               and each holder of the member (`RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS` -- the
#               memory, the file space, the objects, the library, the other
#               apps through `./apps`, the channels); taps all of them, bounded
#               to the app's generation (see `_observer_edges`).
#   pins     -- (GH #916) ONE edge from the declared cell of the app straight
#               onto the generation, `pin` restamped `in_pin` and (GH #949)
#               stamped with the member's round; the generation
#               hands it to the curator of each of its brains. The edge starts
#               at the DECLARED cell, so an app that declares no `pins` has no
#               way in, and a `pin` it emits stays unrouted.
#   candidates
#            -- (GH #949) the push-candidate twin of `pins`: ONE edge from the
#               declared cell onto the generation, `candidate` restamped
#               `in_candidate` and stamped with the member's round; the
#               generation hands it to the curator of each of its brains.
#               Starts at the DECLARED cell for the same reason -- an app that
#               declares no `candidates` has no way in.
#   reads    -- (GH #949) an app's read of its own round off ONE brain's wall:
#               ONE edge from the declared cell onto the generation, `read`
#               restamped `in_read` and stamped `context.read_caller` with the
#               app's name and with the member's round, which the generation
#               hands to the brain
#               `hop.organ` names and that brain to its curator's `./reader`;
#               and the way back, one v-lane `read` per brain from its rim
#               (the lane DOCKS there, `at`) onto the same cell, guarded on
#               that stamp -- an answer reaches the app that asked and no
#               other reader of the generation. A `read` that carries
#               `hop.error_code` is an answer, never a question: every answer
#               of the reader carries one, so a cell that echoes what it got
#               cannot send an answer round again.

#            -- (GH #965) an app's read of the member's RESIDENTS (the memory,
#               the files, the knowledge graph, the objects, the library, the
#               people, the colony's counts, and since GH #976 the last digest
