class DeclarationInvalid(Exception):
    """A declaration outside the vocabulary, named by its field."""

    def __init__(self, reason, field, known):
        Exception.__init__(self, reason)
        self.reason = reason
        self.field = field
        self.known = list(known)


def _one_of(key, values):
    """`has(hop.<key>) && hop.<key> == 'a'`, or `(... || ...)` for several, in
    the order given -- the spelling every hand-drawn install used."""
    if len(values) == 1:
        test = "hop.%s == '%s'" % (key, values[0])
    else:
        test = "(%s)" % " || ".join("hop.%s == '%s'" % (key, v) for v in values)
    return "has(hop.%s) && %s" % (key, test)


def _route_cond(lanes):
    return _one_of("route", lanes)


def _name_cond(names):
    return _one_of("tool_name", names)


def _result_name_cond(names):
    """The name filter of a RESULT: the effective name (`RUN_TOOL_NAME`) --
    the answerer's own `hop.tool_name` when it writes one, else the name the
    call carried out. The residents write none on their results, so a filter
    on `hop.tool_name` alone heard none of them."""
    if len(names) == 1:
        return "(%s) == '%s'" % (RUN_TOOL_NAME, names[0])
    return "(%s) in [%s]" % (RUN_TOOL_NAME, ", ".join("'%s'" % n for n in names))


def _words(value, field, vocab=None):
    """A list of lane words, each from `vocab` when one is given."""
    if not isinstance(value, list) or not all(isinstance(w, str) and w for w in value):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s is a list of lane names" % field, field,
                                 vocab or [])
    for w in value:
        if vocab is not None and w not in vocab:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no %s word %r" % (field, w), field, vocab)
        if vocab is None and set(w) - LANE_ALPHABET:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("%r is not a lane name ([a-z0-9_])" % w,
                                     field, [])
    return value


def _cell(value, field):
    """A cell INSIDE the app, spelled `./<name>` -- a connect point."""
    if (not isinstance(value, str) or not value.startswith("./") or len(value) < 3
            or ".." in value.split("/")):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s names a cell inside the app as ./<name>" % field,
                                 field, [])
    return value


def _word(value, rest, longest):
    """`[a-z][<rest>]{0,longest-1}` -- spelled without `re` on purpose: the
    alphabet is the whole rule."""
    return (isinstance(value, str) and 0 < len(value) <= longest
            and value[0] in LOWER and not set(value[1:]) - rest)


def _check_observes(value, field, default_route):
    """GH #937 -- `{at, tools, route?}`, normalised to all three keys, or
    `DeclarationInvalid` by field. The tools are named, never "all": an observer
    that hears every call would hear the menu of every other app too, and a
    name list is what the condition on the edge is built from."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s is {at, tools, route?}" % field, field, OBSERVE_KEYS)
    for k in value:
        if k not in OBSERVE_KEYS:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no %s key %r" % (field, k), field, OBSERVE_KEYS)
    at = _cell(value.get("at"), field + ".at")
    tools = value.get("tools")
    if not isinstance(tools, list) or not 0 < len(tools) <= OBSERVE_TOOLS_MAX:
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s.tools is a list of 1 to %d tool names"
                                 % (field, OBSERVE_TOOLS_MAX), field + ".tools", [])
    for t in tools:
        if not _word(t, LANE_ALPHABET, 64):
            raise DeclarationInvalid("%r is not a tool name ([a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63})" % (t,),
                                     field + ".tools", [])
    if len(set(tools)) != len(tools):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s.tools names a tool twice" % field, field + ".tools", [])
    route = value.get("route", default_route)
    if not _word(route, LOWER | {"_"}, 40):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%r is not a route ([a-z][a-z_]{0,39})" % (route,),
                                 field + ".route", [])
    return {"at": at, "tools": list(tools), "route": route}


def _check_residents(value):
    """GH #965 -- a non-empty list of resident names out of `RESIDENTS`, each
    once. A name the recipe has no lane for would install green and read
    nothing, so it is refused by field with the names that ARE known."""
    known = sorted(RESIDENTS)
    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
        raise DeclarationInvalid("reads_residents is a list of residents",
                                 "reads_residents", known)
    for i, name in enumerate(value):
        if name not in RESIDENTS:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no resident %r" % (name,),
                                     "reads_residents[%d]" % i, known)
    if len(set(value)) != len(value):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("a resident is named once", "reads_residents", known)
    return list(value)


def _present_residents(p, names):
    """OR-NL-159 (2) -- the residents of `names` the member HAS, in the order
    the declaration names them.

    The recipe reads no tree, so it is TOLD: `residents_present` is the list of
    the member's residents (a name out of `RESIDENTS`, or the resident's cell
    path, with or without `./`) that whoever holds the tree fills in. A
    resident the declaration reads and the member does not have gets no edge:
    an edge onto a node that does not stand is refused at the door as
    `edge_schema`, and that refusal takes the WHOLE installation with it -- a
    presenter that could have shown eight residents shows none. Left out, the
    app's question to it matches no edge and dies at the app's rim, so nothing
    answers it: fail-closed, and the app withdraws what it would have shown.

    A name the recipe has no resident for is ignored rather than refused -- the
    list describes the member (it may well name the member's other apps), it
    is not a word of the app's vocabulary. Absent (`None`) = every resident the
    declaration reads is drawn, exactly as before, EXCEPT a `named_only` one (a
    member app most members lack, GH #976): it is left out -- no edge, no
    refusal -- unless the list names it. An empty list = none."""
    have = p.get("residents_present")
    if have is None:
        return [n for n in names if not RESIDENTS.get(n, {}).get("named_only")]
    if not isinstance(have, list) or not all(isinstance(h, str) for h in have):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("residents_present is a list of the member's residents",
                                 "residents_present", sorted(RESIDENTS))
    cells = {RESIDENTS[n]["cell"]: n for n in RESIDENTS}
    present = set()
    for h in have:
        if h in RESIDENTS:
            present.add(h)
        else:
            cell = h if h.startswith("./") else "./" + h
            if cell in cells:
                present.add(cells[cell])
    return [n for n in names if n in present]


def _resident_edges(app, names, gen, round_, screen):
    """GH #965 -- the app's road to the residents it reads, both ends at its RIM.

    Out: per resident ONE edge `./apps/<app> -> <resident>` on `resident_read`
    naming that resident (`hop.resident`) and carrying the asker's id
    (`hop.op_id`), restamped onto the resident's own read lane. The edge writes
    the asker and its id into the context (the way back is guarded on it) and
    the member's ROUND into `audience_now` AND `audience_set` -- over whatever
    the app wrote, which is why a round an app sets on its own message reaches
    no resident, nor any pull a resident makes on its behalf (the
    `read_caller` pattern, review C-1 of GH #949 and of GH #965).

    Back: per resident and answering route ONE edge `<resident> -> ./apps/<app>`
    guarded on the asker AND on the mark of this read (a `res:` id, the
    `resident` reply-to token), so the answers of a resident's own inner pulls
    stay inside the member (review I-1 of GH #965); restamped
    `resident_answer` with the resident's name, the route it answered on, the
    asker's own id and the ROUND of the answer: the member's, or `["*"]` for
    the colony's counts. The app filters on that round against its screen; it
    never takes the round off the body. Every context key the question wrote
    is deleted there (review I-2 of GH #965).
    """
    here = "./apps/%s" % app
    caller = "'%s'" % app
    round_all = "'[\"*\"]'"
    token = "'%s'" % RESIDENT_TOKEN
    edges = []
    for name in names:
        r = RESIDENTS[name]
        cond = (_route_cond(["resident_read"]) + " && !has(hop.error_code)"
                + " && has(hop.resident) && hop.resident == '%s'" % name
                + " && has(hop.op_id) && hop.op_id != ''")
        set_hop = {"route": "'%s'" % r["lane"]}
        # The round in both keys, the two reply-to marks blank unless this
        # read is theirs (see `RESIDENTS`).
        set_ctx = {"resident_caller": caller, "resident_op": "hop.op_id",
                   "audience_now": round_, "audience_set": round_,
                   "recall_caller": "''", "brief_caller": "''"}
        if r["op_id"]:
            cond += " && has(hop.op)"
            set_hop["op_id"] = "'res:' + hop.op_id"
            set_hop["caller"] = "''"
            mark = "has(hop.op_id) && hop.op_id.startsWith('res:')"
        if r["kind"] == "memory":
            # All five recall keys on every hop, `''` = unset; the query and
            # the tier are the asker's to choose, the round and the channel
            # are not (README memory-hive `in_query`).
            for k in ("recall_query", "memory_tier"):
                set_ctx[k] = "has(hop.%s) ? hop.%s : ''" % (k, k)
            for k in ("recall_as_of", "recall_window_from", "recall_window_to"):
                set_ctx[k] = "''"
            # The channel is the screen the answer is for (the literal an
            # app's screen edge stamps); an app without one reads as itself.
            set_ctx["channel"] = "'%s'" % (screen or "apps/" + app)
            set_ctx["recall_caller"] = token
            mark = "has(hop.recall_caller) && hop.recall_caller == %s" % token
        elif r["kind"] == "tool":
            # A read tool and nothing else: the object hive's writers
            # (`object_set`, `object_confirm`) are a model's, never a screen's.
            cond += " && has(hop.op) && (%s)" % " || ".join(
                "hop.op == '%s'" % t for t in r["tools"])
            set_hop["tool_name"] = "hop.op"
            set_hop["tool_call_id"] = "'res:' + hop.op_id"
            # No speaker: the owner-only answers (`warum`, state) stay closed.
            set_ctx["speaker"] = "''"
            mark = "has(hop.tool_call_id) && hop.tool_call_id.startsWith('res:')"
        elif r["kind"] == "brief":
            set_ctx["asker"] = "'agent:%s'" % gen
            set_ctx["brief_caller"] = token
            mark = "has(context.brief_caller) && context.brief_caller == %s" % token
        edges.append({"from": here, "to": r["cell"], "condition": cond,
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": set_hop, "set_context": set_ctx}})
        answer_round = round_all if r["answer_round"] == RESIDENT_ROUND_ALL else round_
        for route in r["answers"]:
            edges.append({"from": r["cell"], "to": here,
                          "condition": _route_cond([route])
                                       + " && has(context.resident_caller)"
                                         " && context.resident_caller == %s" % caller
                                       + " && " + mark,
                          "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'resident_answer'",
                                                   "resident": "'%s'" % name,
                                                   "resident_status": "'%s'" % route,
                                                   "op_id": "has(context.resident_op)"
                                                            " ? context.resident_op : ''",
                                                   "resident_round": answer_round},
                                       "delete_context": sorted(
                                           set(set_ctx) | set(r.get("inner_keys", ())))}})
    return edges


def _check_shows(value):
    """GH #960 -- `{at}`, closed like an offer. The topics themselves are NOT
    here: they are the app's params and come over the wire as `show_topics`, so
    a block that carries them would be a second copy nobody reads."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("shows is {at}", "shows", SHOW_KEYS)
    for k in value:
        if k not in SHOW_KEYS:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no shows key %r" % k, "shows", SHOW_KEYS)
    at = _cell(value.get("at"), "shows.at")
    # The cell is quoted into the stamp of the answer edge (`show_at`), a CEL
    # literal: the alphabet keeps a quote out of the expression the recipe
    # writes, as it does for a tool name.
    if set(at[2:]) - (LANE_ALPHABET | {"-", "/"}) or "" in at[2:].split("/"):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%r is not a cell name ./[a-z0-9_-]" % (at,), "shows.at", [])
    return at


def _show_edges(app, at):
    """GH #960 -- the app's half of the presenter's road, both at its RIM.

    In: off the container, an `in_show` that names no app (the topics call,
    which every app with `shows` hears -- fan-out is topology, the presenter
    sends once) or names this one (`hop.show_app`, the data call of one topic).
    The container is the source so the order of installation does not matter:
    the presenter puts its question there (`_presenter_edges`), whether it came
    before this app or after it.

    Out: `show_topics` and `show_data` onto the container, where the
    presenter's edge picks them up. The edge stamps `show_app` and `show_at`
    over whatever the app wrote -- the `tool_answerer` / `read_caller` pattern:
    a stamp taken off the message would be a self-report, and an app could
    answer for another. No round is stamped: the round of a screen topic lies
    in its data (`audience_set` per set and row), which the presenter judges
    against its screen; and neither lane is a turn, so nothing here leads into
    `./assistants` or `./firewall`.

    Both edges end at the rim and not on `at`: an app may seal itself
    (`ports: []`), and a member edge onto an interior cell of a sealed hive is
    refused (`hive_port_boundary`). The app routes `. -> <at>` and back in its
    own graph."""
    here = "./apps/%s" % app
    return [
        {"from": "./apps", "to": here,
         "condition": _route_cond(["in_show"])
                      + " && (!has(hop.show_app) || hop.show_app == '' || "
                        "hop.show_app == '%s')" % app},
        {"from": here, "to": "./apps",
         "condition": _route_cond(["show_topics", "show_data"]),
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"show_app": "'%s'" % app, "show_at": "'%s'" % at}}},
    ]


def _presenter_edges():
    """GH #960 -- the presenter's half of the road, drawn with its own
    installation: the question onto the container, every answer back off it,
    and ONE default edge for the question no app took.

    The default is what keeps a presenter alone in its member quiet. It asks
    for topics at every `mutation_committed`, its own installation's too, and
    an `in_show` that reaches a container with no app behind it matches no
    edge and dies there as `hive_no_route`. A default edge is consulted only
    when no regular edge of the sender matched (`edge_table::apply_edges`), so
    it fires exactly when no app with `shows` stands in the member, and it
    hands the question back as an answer of nobody: `show_topics` with an
    empty `show_app`, and the body of the question, which carries no topics.
    A data call names its app and never takes this edge -- an `in_show` for an
    app that is gone dead-letters, which is the truth about it."""
    here = "./apps/%s" % PRESENTER_APP
    return [
        {"from": here, "to": "./apps", "condition": _route_cond(["in_show"])},
        {"from": "./apps", "to": here,
         "condition": _route_cond(["show_topics", "show_data"])},
        {"from": "./apps", "to": here, "default": True,
         "condition": _route_cond(["in_show"])
                      + " && (!has(hop.show_app) || hop.show_app == '')",
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'show_topics'", "show_app": "''",
                                  "show_at": "''"}}},
    ]


def _check_declaration(d):
    if not isinstance(d, dict):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("the declaration is the object `template.json` "
                                 "carries under `app`", "declaration", APP_KEYS)
    for k in d:
        if k not in APP_KEYS:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no declaration key %r" % k, "declaration", APP_KEYS)
    screen = d.get("screen")
    if screen is not None:
        if not isinstance(screen, dict):
            raise DeclarationInvalid("screen is an object", "screen", APP_VOCAB["screen"])
        for k in screen:
            if k not in APP_VOCAB["screen"]:
                raise DeclarationInvalid("no screen key %r" % k, "screen",
                                         APP_VOCAB["screen"])
        out = _words(screen.get("out"), "screen.out", APP_VOCAB["screen.out"])
        if not out:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("an app on a screen draws at least a view",
                                     "screen.out", APP_VOCAB["screen.out"])
        if list(screen.get("back") or []) != list(APP_VOCAB["screen.back"]):
            # A screen answers an app with both or it does not answer it: the
            # member splits `event` and `receipt` on the same owner, and an app
            # that heard one of them would miss the other without a sound.
            raise DeclarationInvalid("screen.back is [\"event\", \"receipt\"]",
                                     "screen.back", APP_VOCAB["screen.back"])
    _words(d.get("listens", []), "listens", APP_VOCAB["listens"])
    offers = d.get("offers", [])
    if not isinstance(offers, list):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("offers is a list", "offers", APP_VOCAB["offers[].kind"])
    for i, o in enumerate(offers):
        field = "offers[%d]" % i
        if not isinstance(o, dict) or o.get("kind") not in APP_VOCAB["offers[].kind"]:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no offer kind %r" % (o.get("kind") if isinstance(o, dict) else o),
                                     field + ".kind", APP_VOCAB["offers[].kind"])
        # Closed like every other block (T4 review minor 1): a key the kind has
        # no rule for would be dropped without a sound.
        allowed = OFFER_KEYS[o["kind"]]
        for k in o:
            if k not in allowed:
                raise DeclarationInvalid("no %s offer key %r" % (o["kind"], k), field,
                                         allowed)
        _cell(o.get("at"), field + ".at")
        if o["kind"] == "tool":
            _words(o.get("tools"), field + ".tools")
            if not o["tools"]:
                raise DeclarationInvalid("a tool offer names its tools", field + ".tools", [])
            for j, t in enumerate(o["tools"]):
                if t in BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES or t.startswith(BUILTIN_TOOL_PREFIXES):
                    raise DeclarationInvalid(
                        "the tool %r is answered by the assistant level, not by an app" % t,
                        "%s.tools[%d]" % (field, j),
                        list(BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES)
                        + ["%s*" % x for x in BUILTIN_TOOL_PREFIXES])
            if "callers" in o:
                _callers(o["callers"], field + ".callers")
        elif not isinstance(o.get("section"), str) or not o["section"]:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("a sidecar offer names its section",
                                     field + ".section", [])
    # GH #981 -- one tool name reaches ONE cell per caller: two offers that
    # hand the same caller the same name would draw two v-lanes on one call.
    # Two offers with disjoint callers may name the same tool.
    seen = {}
    for i, o in enumerate(offers):
        if o["kind"] != "tool":
            continue
        for caller in _offer_callers(o):
            for t in o["tools"]:
                if (caller, t) in seen:
                    raise DeclarationInvalid(
                        "the tool %r is offered to %s twice (offers[%d] and offers[%d])"
                        % (t, caller, seen[(caller, t)], i),
                        "offers[%d].tools" % i, [])
                seen[(caller, t)] = i
    if "observes_tool_calls" in d:
        _check_observes(d["observes_tool_calls"], "observes_tool_calls",
                        OBSERVE_ROUTE["observes_tool_calls"])
    if "observes_tool_results" in d:
        # The string form is the original word (GH #599) and keeps drawing
        # exactly what it drew; the object form is the guarded one (GH #937).
        if isinstance(d["observes_tool_results"], dict):
            _check_observes(d["observes_tool_results"], "observes_tool_results",
                            OBSERVE_ROUTE["observes_tool_results"])
        else:
            _cell(d["observes_tool_results"], "observes_tool_results")
    if "pins" in d:
        _cell(d["pins"], "pins")
    if "candidates" in d:
        _cell(d["candidates"], "candidates")
    if "reads" in d:
        _cell(d["reads"], "reads")
    if "reads_residents" in d:
        _check_residents(d["reads_residents"])
    if "shows" in d:
        _check_shows(d["shows"])
    if "runs" in d:
        _check_runs(d["runs"])
    drives = d.get("drives", [])
    if not isinstance(drives, list):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("drives is a list", "drives", APP_VOCAB["drives[]"])
    for i, dr in enumerate(drives):
        field = "drives[%d]" % i
        if not isinstance(dr, dict) or set(dr) - set(APP_VOCAB["drives[]"]):
            raise DeclarationInvalid("a drive names cell, out and back", field,
                                     APP_VOCAB["drives[]"])
        cell = dr.get("cell")
        if (not isinstance(cell, str) or not cell or cell.startswith("/")
                or ".." in cell.split("/")):
            # A device stands INSIDE the member, beside the container; an
            # absolute path or a way up would be an edge this declaration cannot
            # draw (`ScopeOutOfBounds`).
            raise DeclarationInvalid("drives[].cell is a path inside the member",
                                     field + ".cell", [])
        if [seg for seg in cell.split("/") if seg not in ("", ".")][:1] == ["apps"]:
            # A device stands BESIDE the container. A drive on `./apps` or on an
            # app would draw `./apps -> ./apps/<app>` for every `back` lane and
            # `./apps/<app> -> ./apps` for every `out` lane: the app would hear
            # the `show_data` rows of every other app (meant for the presenter
            # only) and could forge an `in_show` with any `show_app` (review I-1
            # of GH #960).
            raise DeclarationInvalid("drives[].cell is a device beside the apps "
                                     "container, never the container or an app",
                                     field + ".cell", [])
        _words(dr.get("out", []), field + ".out")
        _words(dr.get("back", []), field + ".back")
    return d


def _callers(value, field):
    """GH #981 -- `offers[].callers`: a non-empty list of distinct brains of
    the generation (`OFFER_CALLERS`), or `DeclarationInvalid` by field."""
    if (not isinstance(value, list) or not value
            or not all(isinstance(c, str) for c in value)):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s is a non-empty list of brains of the generation"
                                 % field, field, OFFER_CALLERS)
    for c in value:
        if c not in OFFER_CALLERS:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no brain %r in the generation" % (c,), field,
                                     OFFER_CALLERS)
    if len(set(value)) != len(value):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("%s names a brain twice" % field, field, OFFER_CALLERS)
    return list(value)


def _offer_callers(o):
    """The brains a tool offer is drawn from: its `callers`, else the surfaces."""
    return list(o.get("callers") or SURFACE_CALLERS)


def _check_runs(value):
    """GH #981 -- `runs: {at, brain}`: the cell of the app that hears the run's
    tool results and its end, and the brain the run is handed to."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise DeclarationInvalid("runs is {at, brain}", "runs", RUN_KEYS)
    for k in value:
        if k not in RUN_KEYS:
            raise DeclarationInvalid("no runs key %r" % k, "runs", RUN_KEYS)
    _cell(value.get("at"), "runs.at")
    if value.get("brain") not in RUN_BRAINS:
        raise DeclarationInvalid("runs.brain names the brain a run is handed to, one "
                                 "that answers no channel", "runs.brain", RUN_BRAINS)
    return value


def _run_edges(p, app, runs, gen, round_, inner):
    """GH #981 -- the road of a run: an app hands one brain of its generation a
    turn and hears every tool result of that turn and its end.

    IN: ONE edge from the app's RIM onto the rim of the brain itself,
    `run_turn` restamped `in_turn` with the routing budget restored -- a door,
    like the consult the brain's sibling hands it, and drawn here rather than
    on the assistant level so that no lane of that level is one no occupant
    takes. It carries no `lane`: the app's end sits in the member's app
    container, which declares no contract, and the brain's rim is an address
    of the generation, not an interior node behind a seal. Taken only with a
    `hop.run_id` of `RUN_ID_PATTERN` and below the chain bound
    (`RUN_CHAIN_MAX`) -- a `run_turn` without either matches no edge and
    dead-letters, which is its audit. Everything the brain keys a run on is
    the builder's word, written here: `run_id`, `run_app` (this app, a
    literal -- an app cannot hand another app's run), `run_chain` (the run's
    place in its causal chain, the counter the bound reads), `session_id`
    `run:<app>:<run_id>` (one session per run and app, so meclaw holds no run
    state: how many runs are open is the app's), the generation (`assistant`,
    which addresses the tool results back), and the member's round in
    `audience_set`, `audience_now` and `turn_round` -- the round of a run is
    its member's, never the app's (GH #949 C-1; `audience_now` because the
    graph space reads it first, review C-1 of GH #965). `run_id`, `run_app`
    and `run_chain` are stamped keys: no edge of an app writes them, so an
    app can neither hand another app a forged result nor take a person's
    consult off its surface. `speaker` is written empty: a
    run is said by nobody, and the context the app was woken with may carry a
    person's (GH #979). `consult_class` `run` is a label only: `_call_stamp`
    deletes it on the first tool call, so nothing downstream keys on it.

    THE TOOL RESULTS: a TAP on every road a tool result takes into the
    generation -- off each holder of the member (`RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS`, the
    edges `./<holder> -> ./assistants` restamp it `in_tool`) and off the
    generation's own `./tools` -- guarded on `run_app`, a non-empty `run_id`
    and the brain as `tool_caller`. Restamped `run_tool_result` with
    `run_id`, `answerer`, `ok` and `tool_name` -- the exact name of the call
    (`RUN_TOOL_NAME`, GH #995); `tool_call_id` rides on the hop as the
    answerer wrote it, the body is the result unchanged: the envelope the
    brain gets, ONE message whose `text` is the result. A tap takes nothing
    from the brain: the result still reaches it.

    THE END: ONE edge off the brain's rim, a v-lane `run_answer` that DOCKS
    there (`at` at the assistant), for the brain's `answer`, `error` and
    `model_refused` of the run, restamped `run_answer` with `run_id`, `capped`
    (`round_capped`) and `error` (empty for an answer, `round_stale` for a
    round the idle exit closed, the code for a failure). The answer edges to
    the surfaces exclude a run (`templates/assistant`), so a run never ends in
    an advice."""
    at = inner(runs["at"])
    brain = runs["brain"]
    here = "./apps/%s" % app
    rim = "./assistants/%s" % gen
    mine = (" && has(context.run_app) && context.run_app == '%s'"
            " && has(context.run_id) && context.run_id != ''" % app)
    edges = [{
        "from": here, "to": "%s/%s" % (rim, brain),
        "condition": _route_cond(["run_turn"])
                     + " && has(hop.run_id) && hop.run_id.matches('%s')" % RUN_ID_PATTERN
                     + " && (!has(context.run_chain) || int(context.run_chain) < %d)"
                     % RUN_CHAIN_MAX,
        "modifier": {
            "set_hop": {"route": "'in_turn'"},
            "set_context": {"run_id": "hop.run_id", "run_app": "'%s'" % app,
                            "run_chain": "has(context.run_chain) ? "
                                         "int(context.run_chain) + 1 : 1",
                            "session_id": "'run:%s:' + hop.run_id" % app,
                            "consult_class": "'run'", "assistant": "'%s'" % gen,
                            "audience_set": round_, "audience_now": round_,
                            "turn_round": round_, "speaker": "''", "channel_node": "''", "channel": "''",
                            "col_phase": "''"},
            "delete_context": ["consult_id", "turn_id", "tools_allow", "tools_deny",
                               "tool_caller", "tool_answerer", "offer_tool",
                               "called_tool"],
            "restore_ttl": True}}]
    heard = mine + " && has(context.tool_caller) && context.tool_caller == '%s'" % brain
    present = set(_present_residents(p, [r for _src, r, _a in RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS if r]))
    sources = [(src, answerer) for src, resident, answerer in RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS
               if resident is None or resident in present]
    sources.append((rim + "/tools", "'tools'"))
    for src, answerer in sources:
        edges.append({"from": src, "to": at, "lane": "run_tool_result", "tap": True,
                      "condition": _route_cond(["tool_result"]) + heard,
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {
                          "route": "'run_tool_result'", "run_id": "context.run_id",
                          "answerer": answerer, "tool_name": RUN_TOOL_NAME,
                          "ok": "!has(hop.error_code) || hop.error_code == ''"}}})
    edges.append({
        "from": "%s/%s" % (rim, brain), "to": at, "lane": "run_answer",
        "condition": _route_cond(["answer", "error", "model_refused"]) + mine,
        "modifier": {"set_hop": {
            "route": "'run_answer'", "run_id": "context.run_id",
            "capped": "has(hop.round_capped) && hop.round_capped == '1'",
            "error": "hop.route == 'answer' ? (has(hop.round_stale) && "
                     "hop.round_stale == '1' ? 'round_stale' : '') : "
                     "(has(hop.error_code) && hop.error_code != '' ? "
                     "hop.error_code : hop.route)"}}})
    return edges


def _offers_tool(d):
    """GH #965 -- does the declaration answer tool calls (an offer of kind
    `tool`)? Its results leave in the member's round, so it needs the person."""
    return any(isinstance(o, dict) and o.get("kind") == "tool"
               for o in (d.get("offers") or []))


def _needs_generation(d):
    return (bool(d.get("offers")) or bool(d.get("observes_tool_calls"))
            or bool(d.get("observes_tool_results")) or bool(d.get("pins"))
            or bool(d.get("candidates")) or bool(d.get("reads"))
            or bool(d.get("reads_residents")) or bool(d.get("runs")))


def _call_stamp(caller, gen):
    """The context a surface's tool call carries into an app -- the same stamp
    for an offer and for an observation of it, so the observer reads the call
    exactly as the offering app does."""
    return {"set_context": {"tool_caller": "'%s'" % caller, "assistant": "'%s'" % gen},
            "delete_context": ["col_phase", "consult_class", "consult_id", "tool_answerer",
                               "called_tool"]}


def _observer_edges(p, field, o, app, gen, inner):
    """GH #937 -- the edges of one normalised observation (`_check_observes`).

    An observation is a FAN-OUT, never an interception: every edge here is one
    more regular edge beside the producer's own, so the call still reaches the
    app that offers the tool and the result still reaches the assistant. The
    lane on each edge is the producer's lane (`tool`, `tool_result`) -- that is
    what `v_lane_verdict` matches against the observer's contract --, while
    `set_hop.route` is what the observing cell hears it as.

    Every edge here is a TAP (`"tap": true`, GH #937 review, Important 2): the
    edge table evaluates a sender's edges flat and drops its DEFAULT edges as
    soon as one regular edge matches (`edge_table.rs`, `apply_edges`). The
    surface's own `./<caller> -> ./tools` (route `tool`) is such a default, so
    a regular observer edge on a tool of the generation's own `./tools` would
    TAKE the call instead of overhearing it -- the tool would never run and the
    observer could answer in its place. A tap does not count in that decision,
    so the observation stays a copy whoever offers the tool.

    The result side is bounded to the generation the app is installed for
    (review, Important 1): every holder answers every generation and door of
    the member, and without the guard an observer of generation G would hear
    the results of every other round. The stamp it reads is the one the call
    carried out (`_call_stamp`, the generation's own `tool` exit); a result
    without it is not heard. The edge from the generation's own `./tools` is
    bounded by its path.

    GH #995 -- the result side taps the generation's `./tools` and EVERY
    holder a result enters the generation from (`RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS`, the
    residents among them only if the member has them, like a run's taps): the
    memory, the file space, the objects, the library, the other apps and the
    channels. Before, only the first three were drawn, so an observer of
    `file_ws_exec` installed green and heard nothing. The tools filter and the
    name the observer hears are the effective name (`RUN_TOOL_NAME`): the
    residents write no `tool_name` on their results.
    """
    at = inner(o["at"])
    hop = {"set_hop": {"route": "'%s'" % o["route"]}}
    edges = []
    if field == "observes_tool_calls":
        for caller in SURFACE_CALLERS:
            stamp = _call_stamp(caller, gen)
            stamp.update(hop)
            edges.append({"from": "./assistants/%s/%s" % (gen, caller), "to": at,
                          "lane": "tool", "tap": True,
                          "condition": _route_cond(["tool"]) + " && "
                                       + _name_cond(o["tools"]),
                          "modifier": stamp})
        return edges
    cond = _route_cond(["tool_result"]) + " && " + _result_name_cond(o["tools"])
    this_gen = " && has(context.assistant) && context.assistant == '%s'" % gen
    hop["set_hop"]["tool_name"] = RUN_TOOL_NAME
    present = set(_present_residents(p, [r for _src, r, _a in RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS if r]))
    holders = [src for src, resident, _a in RUN_RESULT_HOLDERS
               if src != "./apps" and (resident is None or resident in present)]
    edges.append({"from": "./assistants/%s/tools" % gen, "to": at, "lane": "tool_result",
                  "tap": True, "condition": cond,
                  "modifier": json.loads(json.dumps(hop))})
    if "./memory-hive" in holders:
        edges.append({"from": "./memory-hive", "to": at, "lane": "tool_result",
                      "tap": True, "condition": cond + this_gen,
                      "modifier": json.loads(json.dumps(hop))})
    # The third producer is every OTHER app. The source is the container, not
    # `./apps/<x>`: an observer installed before the app it hears would
    # otherwise miss it, so the install order does not matter. The answering
    # app is named by `context.tool_answerer` (its own exit stamps it), which
    # also keeps an app from hearing its own results.
    edges.append({"from": "./apps", "to": at, "lane": "tool_result", "tap": True,
                  "condition": cond + this_gen + " && has(context.tool_answerer)"
                               " && context.tool_answerer != '%s'" % app,
                  "modifier": json.loads(json.dumps(hop))})
    # GH #995 -- the other holders, after the three drawn since GH #937.
    for src in holders:
        if src == "./memory-hive":
            continue
        edges.append({"from": src, "to": at, "lane": "tool_result", "tap": True,
                      "condition": cond + this_gen,
                      "modifier": json.loads(json.dumps(hop))})
    return edges


# --- the credential road of an app (GH #976) -------------------------------
#
# An app's llm cell spends a provider key like a brain does, so it takes the
# same road (GH #560): the key lives in the member's own `./access`, the cell
# holds `credential_grant_id` and an EMPTY `api_key` -- the switch, because the
# llm cell asks only while it holds no credential -- and two v-lanes join the
# cell and the broker. The installation stands at the member already (the
# scope of every `install_app` declaration), so the road needs no wide form:
# the edges are the member's, the cell's own template names it as the connect
# point (`at`) of both lanes, and the grant rides in the same diff as the node,
# because `credential_grant_id` is immutable and the grant has to exist before
# the cell that names it ever asks.
#
# WHICH cells spend a grant is a fact of the app's template, known here by
# name for the one app that has one, like `_presenter_registry` knows the
# decider: the recipe reads no tree, and a declaration key would make every
# recipe that has not learnt it refuse the presenter's block. A `credential`
# for an app with no such cell is refused by name, never dropped -- the wish
# would read like one answered and the app would still pull its key from
# `.env`.
#
# The requester is `app:<app>/<cell>` and the handle `<app>-<cell>` as the
# consumer: one grant per consumer, so no brain of the member and no other app
# can be handed this cell's sealed box.
#
# The list is keyed by the TEMPLATE, and the app must carry the template's name:
# an app called `presenter` grown from another template that happens to have a
# `decide` cell gets no grant (Y fix round 1, M-1).
# GH #1061: the cells come from CREDENTIAL_CONSUMERS -- one table for the levels
# and the apps -- restricted to the templates that are installed as apps.
APP_CREDENTIAL_TEMPLATES = ("presenter", "display")


def _app_credential(app, cred, template):
    """[(cell, handle, requester)] for every cell of `app` that spends a grant."""
    name = _template_name(template)
    rows = (CREDENTIAL_CONSUMERS.get(name)
            if name == app and name in APP_CREDENTIAL_TEMPLATES else None)
    if not rows:
        raise DeclarationInvalid("app %r (template %r) has no cell that spends a grant"
                                 % (app, name),
                                 "credential", sorted(APP_CREDENTIAL_TEMPLATES))
    out = []
    for cell, kind in rows:
        ref = _credential_ref(cred, kind)
        if ref:
            out.append((cell, _grant_handle(ref, cred["subject"],
                                            "%s-%s" % (app, cell.replace("/", "-"))),
                        "app:%s/%s" % (app, cell)))
    return out


def _app_credential_edges(app, cred, template):
    """The two v-lanes per cell, in the form `_credential_edges` draws."""
    edges = []
    for cell, handle, requester in _app_credential(app, cred, template):
        at = "./apps/%s/%s" % (app, cell)
        edges.append({
            "from": at, "to": CREDENTIAL_BROKER,
            "lane": "credential_request",
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'credential_request'",
            "modifier": {
                "set_hop": {"route": "'in_invoke'"},
                "set_context": {"requester": "'%s'" % requester}}})
        edges.append({
            "from": CREDENTIAL_BROKER, "to": at,
            "lane": "in_sealed",
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'ack' && "
                         "has(hop.operation) && hop.operation == 'vault.deliver'"
                         " && has(hop.grant_id) && hop.grant_id == '%s'" % handle,
            "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_sealed'"}}})
    return edges


def _app_credential_rows(app, cred, now, template):
    """The grants and their birth events, through the mutation door."""
    grants, events = [], []
    for cell, handle, requester in _app_credential(app, cred, template):
        grants.append({
            "grant_id": handle,
            "requester": requester,
            "capability": "credential.read",
            "subject": cred["subject"],
            "scope": {"actions": ["vault.deliver"]},
            "cred_ref": cred["cred_ref"],
            "purpose": "authenticate the %s app's %s cell against the provider"
                       % (app, cell),
            "issued_at": now,
            "expires_at": cred["expires_at"],
            "rule_id": cred.get("rule_id") or "credential-read",
            "constraints": {"rate_per_min": int(cred.get("rate_per_min")
                                                or CREDENTIAL_RATE_PER_MIN)}})
        events.append({
            "id": "ev-app-%s-%s" % (app, cell),
            "grant_id": handle,
            "event": "granted",
            "at": now,
            "actor": "operator",
            "reason_code": "",
            "detail": {"why": "seeded with the app: credential_grant_id "
                              "is immutable, so the grant has to exist before "
                              "the cell that names it ever asks"}})
    return [{"target": "./access/store", "table": "grants", "rows": grants},
            {"target": "./access/store", "table": "grant_events",
             "rows": events}]


def _app_credential_overrides(given, app, cred, template):
    """Both params on every spending cell, merged into what the wish set."""
    out = dict(given or {})
    for cell, handle, _requester in _app_credential(app, cred, template):
        own = dict(out.get(cell) or {})
        own["api_key"] = ""
        own["credential_grant_id"] = handle
        out[cell] = own
    return out


def install_app(p, settings=None):
    d = _check_declaration(p["declaration"])
    app = p["app"]
    if app == PRESENTER_APP and "shows" in d:
        # The presenter's question goes to every app with `shows`; one of its
        # own would bring the question back to the presenter as an app.
        raise DeclarationInvalid("the presenter shows nothing of its own: its "
                                 "topics question would come back to itself",
                                 "shows", [])
    here = "./apps/%s" % app
    screen = p["screen"]
    # GH #967.1 -- the generation is written into the round literal below.
    gen = (_round_name(p["generation"], "params.generation", GENERATION_QUESTION)
           if _needs_generation(d) else None)
    inner = lambda at: here + at[1:]
    edges = []

    # GH #949 (review C-1, I-1) -- the ROUND an app pins, pushes candidates and
    # reads in is its member's, stamped HERE on the one edge each of those three
    # lanes leaves the app by, and never the app's own word. The context an
    # app's message carries is written by the app's own template, and nothing
    # in the substrate stops an edge inside it from `set_context: {audience_set:
    # ...}` (`ROUND_CONTEXT_KEYS`, `cel_eval.rs`, guards deletion only): a round
    # taken off the message is a self-report. `["agent:<a>"]` covers every row
    # the agent is part of; a group round lets a candidate or a pin learnt in
    # the one-to-one chat into the group past `audience_widened`, which checks
    # against the very round the app declared. The edge belongs to the builder
    # and runs after every edge of the app, so its stamp overwrites whatever the
    # app said -- the `read_caller` / `tool_answerer` pattern. The literal is
    # the one `_channel_level` stamps on the member's own turns, the agent being
    # the generation the app is installed for: an app reaches at most what its
    # member may see, and an app woken by its own timer (a fresh root with no
    # context, `timer/cell.rs`) has a round as well.
    #
    # GH #965 (review N-1, OR-DP.M.18) -- the round a tool RESULT leaves in is
    # the same literal, for the same reason: a round the call edge parked in the
    # app's context (`offer_round`) could be rewritten by any inner edge of the
    # app on its way out, and an object-form observer of another app would then
    # hear the result in `["*"]`. Only what the boundary writes is the
    # builder's word, so an app that answers a tool call names its member too.
    round_ = None
    if (d.get("pins") or d.get("candidates") or d.get("reads")
            or d.get("reads_residents") or _offers_tool(d) or d.get("runs")):
        person = _person(p, APP_PERSON_QUESTION)
        round_ = "'[\"agent:%s\",\"member:%s\"]'" % (gen, person)

    listens = list(d.get("listens") or [])
    if "turn" in listens:
        edges.append({"from": "./firewall", "to": "./apps",
                      "condition": _route_cond(["pass"]),
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'turn'"},
                                   "delete_context": ["fw_body", "fw_now",
                                                      "fw_phase", "store_origin"]}})
    if "answer" in listens:
        edges.append({"from": "./assistants", "to": "./apps",
                      "condition": _route_cond(["answer"])})
        edges.append({"from": "./assistants", "to": ".",
                      "condition": _route_cond(["answer"])
                      + " && (!has(context.channel_node) || context.channel_node == '')",
                      "modifier": {"delete_context": ["tool_answerer"]}})
    if "partial" in listens:
        edges.append({"from": "./channels", "to": "./apps",
                      "condition": _route_cond(["partial"])})
    if "close" in listens:
        edges.append({"from": "./assistants", "to": "./apps",
                      "condition": _route_cond(["write"]),
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_close'"},
                                   "set_context": {
                                       k: "has(context.%s) ? context.%s : ''" % (k, k)
                                       for k in ("session_id", "audience_set", "channel")}}})
    if listens:
        edges.append({"from": "./apps", "to": here,
                      "condition": _route_cond(["in_close" if w == "close" else w
                                                for w in listens])})

    offers = list(d.get("offers") or [])
    for o in offers:
        if o["kind"] == "sidecar":
            edges.append({"from": "./apps", "to": here,
                          "condition": _route_cond(["sidecar"])
                          + " && has(hop.section) && hop.section == '%s'" % o["section"]})

    if d.get("screen"):
        edges.append({"from": "./apps", "to": here,
                      "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || "
                                   "hop.route == 'receipt') && has(hop.owner) && "
                                   "hop.owner.contains('/apps/%s/')" % app})
        edges.append({"from": here, "to": "./apps",
                      "condition": _route_cond(list(d["screen"]["out"]) + ["error"]),
                      "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % screen,
                                                   "channel": "'%s'" % screen}}})

    if offers:
        tool = any(o["kind"] == "tool" for o in offers)
        edges.append({"from": here, "to": "./apps",
                      "condition": _route_cond(["tool_schemas"]),
                      "modifier": {"set_context": {"tool_answerer": "'%s'" % app}}})
        names = []
        for o in offers:
            if o["kind"] == "tool":
                names.extend(t for t in o["tools"] if t not in names)
        if names:
            # GH #963 review N-1 -- a result leaves the app in the words of the
            # CALL and of the builder, never in its own: the name is restamped
            # from what the call edge stamped on the way in (`offer_tool`,
            # below), the generation is the one the app is installed for, and
            # the round is its member's (`round_` above) -- a literal of this
            # edge, which no inner edge of the app can rewrite (OR-DP.M.18: a
            # round parked in the context by the call edge could be). The app
            # wrote all three itself before, so it could hand an object-form
            # observer of another app (`./apps` leg of `_observer_edges`) a
            # `web_search` result in any round. The name is bound to the app's
            # own offer besides: whatever its inner edges write into
            # `offer_tool`, only a tool it offers leaves -- the producer stamp
            # `templates/tools` gives its results since GH #937. A `tool_result`
            # that answers no call of a surface leaves nothing.
            edges.append({"from": here, "to": "./apps",
                          "condition": _route_cond(["tool_result"])
                                       + " && has(context.offer_tool) && ("
                                       + " || ".join("context.offer_tool == '%s'" % t
                                                     for t in names) + ")",
                          "modifier": {"set_hop": {"tool_name": "context.offer_tool"},
                                       "set_context": {"tool_answerer": "'%s'" % app,
                                                       "assistant": "'%s'" % gen,
                                                       "audience_set": round_},
                                       "delete_context": ["offer_tool"]}})
        # GH #981 -- per caller of any tool offer (the surfaces first, the
        # order every install before `callers` drew): its tool v-lanes, then
        # ONE menu tick per cell that offers it something. A surface ticks a
        # sidecar's cell as well, as it always did; a declaration without
        # `callers` draws exactly the edges it drew before.
        callers = [c for c in OFFER_CALLERS
                   if c in SURFACE_CALLERS
                   or any(o["kind"] == "tool" and c in _offer_callers(o) for o in offers)]
        for caller in callers:
            stamp = _call_stamp(caller, gen)
            src = "./assistants/%s/%s" % (gen, caller)
            mine = [o for o in offers
                    if o["kind"] == "tool" and caller in _offer_callers(o)]
            cells = []
            for o in offers:
                if ((o in mine or (o["kind"] == "sidecar" and caller in SURFACE_CALLERS))
                        and o["at"] not in cells):
                    cells.append(o["at"])
            for o in mine:
                # The call's own word, kept for the way out (review N-1):
                # the tool it names. Its round is not kept -- the way out
                # stamps the member's (OR-DP.M.18).
                call = json.loads(json.dumps(stamp))
                call["set_context"]["offer_tool"] = "hop.tool_name"
                edges.append({"from": src, "to": inner(o["at"]), "lane": "tool",
                              "condition": _route_cond(["tool"]) + " && "
                                           + _name_cond(o["tools"]),
                              "modifier": call})
            for at in cells:
                edges.append({"from": src, "to": inner(at), "lane": "schemas",
                              "condition": _route_cond(["schemas"]),
                              "modifier": json.loads(json.dumps(stamp))})

    if d.get("observes_tool_calls"):
        o = _check_observes(d["observes_tool_calls"], "observes_tool_calls",
                            OBSERVE_ROUTE["observes_tool_calls"])
        edges.extend(_observer_edges(p, "observes_tool_calls", o, app, gen, inner))

    observed = d.get("observes_tool_results")
    if isinstance(observed, dict):
        o = _check_observes(observed, "observes_tool_results",
                            OBSERVE_ROUTE["observes_tool_results"])
        edges.extend(_observer_edges(p, "observes_tool_results", o, app, gen, inner))
    elif observed:
        # The string form (GH #599): every result of the two producers, as it
        # comes. Kept byte for byte -- installed apps carry these edges.
        at = inner(observed)
        for src in ("./assistants/%s/tools" % gen, "./memory-hive"):
            edges.append({"from": src, "to": at, "lane": "tool_result",
                          "condition": _route_cond(["tool_result"])})

    if d.get("pins"):
        edges.append({"from": inner(d["pins"]), "to": "./assistants/%s" % gen,
                      "condition": _route_cond(["pin"]),
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_pin'"},
                                   "set_context": {"audience_set": round_}}})

    if d.get("candidates"):
        edges.append({"from": inner(d["candidates"]), "to": "./assistants/%s" % gen,
                      "condition": _route_cond(["candidate"]),
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_candidate'"},
                                   "set_context": {"audience_set": round_}}})

    if d.get("reads"):
        # GH #949 -- the question onto the generation, stamped with the asker:
        # the edge writes `read_caller`, so an app cannot answer for another,
        # and the member's round (`round_` above), so it cannot read another.
        cell = inner(d["reads"])
        edges.append({"from": cell, "to": "./assistants/%s" % gen,
                      "condition": _route_cond(["read"]) + " && !has(hop.error_code)",
                      "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_read'"},
                                   "set_context": {"read_caller": "'%s'" % app,
                                                   "audience_set": round_}}})
        for organ in READ_ORGANS:
            edges.append({"from": "./assistants/%s/%s" % (gen, organ), "to": cell,
                          "lane": "read",
                          "condition": _route_cond(["read"])
                                       + " && has(context.read_caller)"
                                         " && context.read_caller == '%s'" % app,
                          "modifier": {"delete_context": ["read_caller"]}})

    if d.get("runs"):
        edges.extend(_run_edges(p, app, d["runs"], gen, round_, inner))

    if d.get("reads_residents"):
        # OR-NL-159 (2) -- only the residents the member has (`_present_residents`).
        edges.extend(_resident_edges(app, _present_residents(p, d["reads_residents"]),
                                     gen, round_, screen))

    if d.get("shows"):
        edges.extend(_show_edges(app, d["shows"]["at"]))
    if app == PRESENTER_APP:
        edges.extend(_presenter_edges())

    for dr in d.get("drives") or []:
        cell = dr["cell"] if dr["cell"].startswith("./") else "./" + dr["cell"]
        for lane in dr.get("out") or []:
            edges.append({"from": here, "to": cell, "condition": _route_cond([lane]),
                          "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_%s'" % lane}}})
        for lane in dr.get("back") or []:
            edges.append({"from": cell, "to": here, "condition": _route_cond([lane])})

    # GH #979 (OR-NL.I.11) -- an app holds no privilege: the door refuses this
    # node when a cell of its template declares `contract.parks_context`
    # (the one cell whose `ctx_speaker` may be restored on an edge).
    node = {"name": "apps/%s" % app, "template": p["template"],
            "privileged": False}
    if isinstance(p.get("override_params"), dict):
        node["override_params"] = p["override_params"]
    # GH #976 -- the grant way, opt-in like the level's (`credential`). The
    # edges come LAST, behind the app's own, and the grants ride in the diff.
    credential = p.get("credential")
    if credential:
        node["override_params"] = _app_credential_overrides(
            node.get("override_params"), app, credential, p["template"])
        edges = edges + _app_credential_edges(app, credential, p["template"])
    if p.get("birth"):
        node["birth"] = p["birth"]
    ctx = p.get("ctx") if isinstance(p.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
    out = [{"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": ctx,
            "diff": {"add_nodes": [node], "add_edges": edges}}]
    if credential:
        now = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
               .strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"))
        out[0]["diff"]["seed_rows"] = _app_credential_rows(app, credential, now,
                                                            p["template"])
    # GH #963 / PE-DP-11 -- after the app's own entry, so the node the
    # announcement leaves from is born before its edges are judged.
    return out + _presenter_registry(p, settings)


RENDER = {"rewire_edge": rewire_edge, "add_node": add_node,
          "attach_drain": attach_drain, "grow_level": grow_level,
          "install_app": install_app}


# --- the screen a member always gets (GH #543, ruling R-0904-4) -------------
#
# A person in this substrate is the thing that HAS input and output devices.
# Whether they use them is a second question; that they have them is not one at
# all -- so a member wish grows the person AND the screen it speaks through and
# the application that draws on it. There is no `screen: false`: `classify`
# drops a falsy key, so a tri-state would be indistinguishable from a wish that
# never mentioned it, and the ruling has no third state to distinguish anyway.
#
# The NAMES are fixed here for the same reason the container of a level is
# (`LEVELS`): a member does not stand in `./people` in one colony and
# `./members` in another, and a screen that can be renamed is a wish choosing
# again. What is NOT fixed here is which TEMPLATE fills them, or what the
# screen's door is called -- those are the builder's own configuration
# (`doc["params"]`),
# because the builder is part of the OS and the OS is what hands out what is
# system-near (ADR-0022).
MEMBER_SCREEN = "display"
MEMBER_APP = "colony-view"

# The mount grammar, as the substrate holds it
# (`crates/meclaw-colony/src/surfaces/mod.rs`): `[a-z0-9-]{1,64}`, and none of
# the names a route on the same listener already answers. It is NARROWER than a
# node name -- nothing stops a member being called `Alex` or `alex_1` -- so the
# rendered door is checked here rather than at the door.
MOUNT_MAX = 64
MOUNT_ALPHABET = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-")
RESERVED_MOUNTS = ("colony", "messages", "health", "ui", "live", "@client")


class MountUnrenderable(Exception):
    """The name that came out of `screen_mount` is not a mount.

    Refused HERE, by name, and nothing is rendered: a manifest rolls forward
    with no rollback, so a wish that got past this point would commit the PERSON
    and then have its screen refused at the door -- with a message that names the
    grammar and never names the member. That is the half-act GH #585 and GH #543
    exist to prevent, re-entered through a name.

    It wears `wish_incomplete`, the code the design lane already uses for a build
    that stopped because it was not told enough, with the missing thing named in
    words a human can answer: the answer here is a different member name.
    """

    def __init__(self, mount, pattern):
        Exception.__init__(self, mount)
        self.mount = mount
        self.pattern = pattern


# The defaults, used when the instance overrides nothing.
DEFAULT_SETTINGS = {"member_screen_template": "display@2.10.6",
                    "member_app_template": "colony-view@1.2.0",
                    "screen_mount": "{member}-display",
                    "model_registry_scope": ""}


def member_devices(p, settings):
    """The devices half of a member wish: its screen, and the app on it.

    TWO declarations and not one, because a screen stands in `channels` and an
    app in `apps`: two containers are two scope roots since GH #503, and a
    declaration has exactly one. They travel BEHIND the person in the same
    manifest because they are one decision -- a screen nobody draws on and an
    app with nothing to draw on are each half an act, and a person without
    either is the silent failure GH #585 measured.

    The MOUNT is `screen_mount` with `{member}` filled in, written as
    `override_params` on the screen's own node. It is not in the wish and not in
    the template: since `web@2.0.0` a display has no port and answers under a
    name on the colony's one listener, and a name inside one listener is what
    the OS allocates exactly once (GH #655).
    """
    # The member's own PATH, which is not the scope the wish named: a member
    # wish says "under /os/orgs/acme" and the person stands one storey below
    # that, in the container the level declares itself at (GH #503). Read off
    # `Place` rather than spelled again, so the two cannot disagree.
    container, _render, _extra = LEVELS["member"]
    member = "%s/%s" % (Place(container, True).scope(p["scope"]), p["name"])
    pattern = str(settings["screen_mount"])
    mount = pattern.replace("{member}", p["name"])
    if (not mount or len(mount) > MOUNT_MAX or mount in RESERVED_MOUNTS
            or set(mount) - MOUNT_ALPHABET):
        raise MountUnrenderable(mount, pattern)
    screen_wish = {"scope": member, "level": "screen",
                   "name": MEMBER_SCREEN,
                   "template": settings["member_screen_template"],
                   "override_params": {"web": {"mount": mount}}}
    # GH #1061: the screen's judge spends the member's credential like the
    # member's own cells do -- the same wish, one grant per consumer.
    if p.get("credential"):
        screen_wish["credential"] = p["credential"]
    screen = grow_level(screen_wish)
    app = grow_level({"scope": member, "level": "app", "name": MEMBER_APP,
                      "template": settings["member_app_template"],
                      "screen": MEMBER_SCREEN})
    return screen + app


def read_settings(params):
    """The four values an instance may set, defaulted where it set none."""
    out = dict(DEFAULT_SETTINGS)
    for key in DEFAULT_SETTINGS:
        value = (params or {}).get(key)
        if value not in (None, ""):
            out[key] = value
    return out

# GH #543 -- a member wish renders the person AND the screen and the app that
# person always gets, in that order: the devices draw into `<member>/channels`
# and `<member>/apps`, scopes only the person creates.
#
# GH #585 -- and they leave as ONE SUBMISSION. The order between them is
# semantics, and a front has no ordering across two submissions handed over in
# the same turn: measured on a fresh colony, the devices reached the door first
# and were refused with `edge_schema` for a scope that did not exist yet, while
# the person committed behind them -- a member without a screen and without an
# app, and a wish that reported success. Inside ONE manifest the order is the
# door's to keep: the colony rolls a manifest off entry by entry through the
# very `handle_mutation` a single body takes, so an entry is judged against the
# tree the entries in front of it just grew (measured in
# `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh585_a_member_wish_is_one_submission.rs`). The
# roll-forward still has no rollback, so the order is not a preference; it is
# now inside the one document that carries it.
#
# `doc["params"]` is read HERE and at the `grow_level` and `install_app` calls above, and nowhere
# else, and it is the only thing this cell reads beyond its own stdin: no
# network, no disk, no retrieval. What it says is which template fills the two
# devices, what the screen's door on the listener is called, and -- since GH
# #855 -- the container scope the colony's model registry pushes into -- the
# instance's own configuration, set with `override_params` on the builder.
manifests = [decls]
if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("level") == "member":
    settings = read_settings(doc.get("params"))
    try:
        manifests = [decls + member_devices(params, settings)]
    except MountUnrenderable as e:
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
            "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "wish_incomplete",
                       "recipe": recipe},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                          "text": json.dumps({

                                        "at %r, and that is not a mount: a mount "

                                        "and none of colony, messages, health, "

                                        "name -- the member's own, and the "
                                        "builder's `screen_mount` (%r): name the "
                                        "member something that renders one, or "

                              "missing": ["params.name",
                                          "params.screen_mount"]})}]}))

left_out_note = ""
if REGISTRY_LEFT_OUT:
    said = ", ".join("%s (%s)" % (b["cell_path"], b["reason"]) for b in REGISTRY_LEFT_OUT)
    sys.stderr.write("recipes: the model registry's road leaves out %s\n" % said)

out = []
for one in manifests:

    out.append({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "manifest_class": "fast",
                   "manifest_sha256": sha, "declaration_count": len(one)},
        "manifest": one,
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "%s: %d declaration(s), scope %s%s" % (

# GH #480 -- the fast lane writes down what a refusal will need, and it is the
# same two rows the design lane already writes.
#
# A refused submission comes back on `in_receipt`, which arrives on a FOREIGN
# chain by construction: `templates/submit/gate` renders the receipt off its own
# remembered row, so nothing of this build's context survives the round trip.
# `weave` recovers a composed build from two rows -- `normalise`'s digest
# binding, which says who owns those bytes, and the caller row, which says which
# door the answer goes to. A recipe wrote neither, so a refused fast-lane build
# ended as `build_unknown` and was delivered into `./orgs` rather than to the
# operator that asked (measured: `template_missing`, GH #480).
#
# The build id IS the digest. A fast-lane build has no other identity -- no
# composer opened a round to mint one -- and the digest is the one handle that
# survives the submitter's chain, because the submitter parks and pops a
# submission under it.
#
# `build_lane` is the third thing the row says, and it is the reason the row can
# be read at all: a model-free build has no composer, no thread and no question,
# so its refusal must NOT enter the repair machine. `weave` reads the marker off
# this row and takes the short road instead -- name the code, answer the door.
#
# Nothing is written for a REFUSED recipe: a build that produced no bytes has no
# digest to be refused under, and a row nobody can reach is a slate that only
# grows. And nothing is written when the context names NO caller at all -- the
# same guard `weave` parks its own row under (`names_a_caller`). There is no door
# to recover then, because none was ever stamped, and a slate written for a build
# nobody is waiting on is a table that only grows.
ctx = ((doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
caller = {k: str(ctx.get(k) or "") for k in CALLER_KEYS}
names_a_caller = any(caller.values())
caller["build_lane"] = "recipe"
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def parked(build_id, slot, role, turn):
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": slot,
            "text": json.dumps({
                "operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
                "row": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": 0, "role": role,
                        "turn": turn, "fired": 0, "recorded_at": now}})}


# `operation` is `bind` and not `recipe`: BOTH `./recipes -> .` edges match on
# `hop.operation == 'recipe'`, so a binding wearing that operation would leave
# the hive as a second answer to the same wish.
#
# ONE PAIR PER MANIFEST. `weave` finds the caller row by `build_id == <digest>`,
# and a manifest is refused or committed under its own digest, so a build that
# wrote no pair for a manifest it emitted would leave that manifest's refusal
# with no door to answer to -- the exact `build_unknown` failure GH #480
# measured for the fast lane as a whole. Since GH #585 a member wish emits one
# manifest, so it writes one pair; the loop stays because the rule is per
# manifest and not per wish.
if names_a_caller:
    for one in manifests:
        one_sha = digest(one)
        out.append({
            "header": {"route": "bind", "operation": "bind",
                       "manifest_sha256": one_sha},
            "messages": [parked(one_sha, "w-fast-caller", "caller",
                                json.dumps(caller)),
                         parked(one_sha, "w-fast-bind", "manifest", one_sha)]})
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))

member_screen_template.description: The template the screen every member gets is instantiated from (GH #543). It lives on the BUILDER and not in the wish: a member does not choose whether it has a screen, and the recipe does not choose what fills one -- a template is a catalogue question. Colony-wide, which in a colony carrying one organisation is the same statement as `the org assigns it`; a real per-org surface does not exist in the substrate (org is a namespace, `HiveParams` is deny_unknown_fields, and no read endpoint hands params out).

member_app_template.description: The template the application that draws on that screen is instantiated from (GH #543). Same argument, same place: a screen nobody draws on is half an act, so the two are configured together and rendered together.

screen_mount.description: The name a member's screen is reached under on the colony's one listener (GH #543, GH #645, GH #655). `{member}` is replaced by the member's own name, so the screen of `alex` is at `/alex-display/`. A display owns no port since `web@2.0.0`; the OS hands out the NAME, because a name inside one listener is the system-near thing a colony has to allocate exactly once (ADR-0022). What comes out of the pattern has to be a mount -- `[a-z0-9-]{1,64}`, and none of `colony`, `messages`, `health`, `ui`, `live`, `@client` -- which is narrower than a node name: a member wish whose name does not render one is refused here as `wish_incomplete`, before anything is rendered, rather than at the door with the person already committed.

model_registry_scope.description: The container scope the colony's `llm-registry` pushes model packages into (GH #855), or empty for a tree that carries no registry. Set, a `grow_level assistant` whose generation lies under it renders a SECOND declaration at that scope: one push edge per brain (`talky`, `talky-chat`, `cogny`, and since GH #877 the curator summarizer behind each rim) onto the composite's `in_model` door, addressed by `hop.subscriber`, and one edge that turns every mutation receipt reaching the generation into the announcement of its brains, which the registry makes subscribers of. Empty, nothing extra is rendered and every brain keeps its start value. `meclaw-os` sets it to `/os/orgs` on its builder ref, because that is where its shell carries the registry's `update` lane.

description.purpose: The fast lane: five predefined recipes rendered straight from their parameters into a manifest, with its sha256 digest. No model, no network, no disk -- what leaves here is a string built out of a dict. The fourth is grow_level, which renders the transit edge set a composition level gives a new child: it is the same set every time, so it is a table here rather than a paragraph a model rewrites per build. The counts live in the README, once, and a test derives them from this renderer. Two things ride BESIDE that set: a `birth` state written top-level on the node -- the door's own vocabulary, and a channel is rendered `inactive` because a connector opens its upstream the moment it has a task -- and, for an assistant and only when the wish asks, the identity door: the push edge from the member's own affinity record plus the receipt drain beside it. Since GH #543 a MEMBER wish renders the person AND the screen and the application that person always gets, the screen under the mount `screen_mount` renders from the member's own name; since GH #585 the three ride in ONE manifest, in dependency order, because two submissions handed to a front in the same turn have no order at all and the devices draw into scopes only the person creates. The fifth is install_app (GH #599): an application is installed from the block its template carries under `app` -- screen, listens, offers, observes_tool_results, drives -- handed over in the wish as `declaration`, because this cell reads nothing but its stdin; the recipe draws the member's observer edges, the binding to the app, the tool and menu v-lanes from both surfaces of the generation, the observed tool results and a device's road, and refuses a word outside that vocabulary as `app_declaration_invalid`, naming the field and what is known.
description.use_when: Behind `classify` on hop.route == 'recipe', when the caller named a recipe and its parameters are complete.
description.not_in_scope: No inference, no retrieval, no application. No template CHOICE either: grow_level renders edges and is TOLD which template to instantiate -- by the wish, or, for the screen a member always gets, by its own configuration -- because what a level should be filled with is a catalogue question and the catalogue is the librarian's. And no LOOKUP of any kind: the screen's name comes from `screen_mount` with the member's own name filled in, and a pattern that renders something the mount grammar refuses is `wish_incomplete`. No subscription ROW either: writing one is a store write and not a mutation declaration, so it stays a `subscribe` op through affinity's own gate -- what is rendered here is the graph that row will need. And no rollback to lean on: the order of the declarations is semantics, because a manifest rolls forward and stops at the first refusal. And no ROUND to invent: the audience a grown channel's turns are spoken in is read off the wish's own `ctx` (`member_person`) and a wish that does not name it is asked, because a round is provenance and a wrong one blanks the whole memory behind a gate that is working exactly as specified (GH #517).
